definitions.explanation: To catch one's foot on something and lose balance while walking or running. The obstacle causes an unintended forward motion that may or may not result in a fall.

definitions.gloss: to encounter an obstacle; to hit a snag
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, to encounter an unexpected problem or difficulty that hinders progress in work, life, or a project.

examples.japanese: ⟦{石|いし}→石：02177_ishi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧つまずいて⟦{転|ころ}んだ→転ぶ：00863_korobu⟧。
examples.english: I tripped on a stone and fell.

examples.japanese: ⟦{暗|くら}い→暗い：00647_kurai⟧⟦{廊下|ろうか}→廊下：05005_rouka⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧つまずかない⟦ように→ように：noentry⟧⟦{気|き}をつけて→気をつける：09771_kiwotsukeru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please be careful not to trip in the dark hallway.

examples.japanese: ⟦{段差|だんさ}→段差：14742_dansa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧つまずいて⟦{足首|あしくび}→足首：00918_ashikubi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦ひねって→捻る：00102_hineru⟧⟦しまった→仕舞う：03064_shimau⟧。
examples.english: I tripped on a step and twisted my ankle.

examples.japanese: ⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦プロジェクト→プロジェクト：06764_purojekuto⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{予算|よさん}→予算：03663_yosan⟧⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧つまずいた。
examples.english: The new project hit a snag due to budget issues.

examples.japanese: ⟦{出|で}だし→出だし：30703_dedashi⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧つまずいて⟦しまった→仕舞う：03064_shimau⟧。
examples.english: I stumbled right from the start.

examples.japanese: ⟦{受験勉強|じゅけんべんきょう}→受験勉強：09977_jukenbenkyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{数学|すうがく}→数学：01442_suugaku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧つまずいて、⟦{塾|じゅく}→塾：04702_juku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{通|かよ}い→通う：01217_kayou⟧⟦{始|はじ}めた→始める：00531_hajimeru⟧。
examples.english: I was struggling with math in my exam prep, so I started going to a cram school.

notes:
PARTICLE: the thing you trip over takes ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧, not ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ — ⟦{石|いし}→石：02177_ishi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧つまずく. In the figurative sense the same ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ marks the subject or stage that defeated you (⟦{数学|すうがく}→数学：01442_suugaku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧つまずく), while ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧ marks the cause or the point at which things went wrong.

WRITING:
Can be written {躓|つまず}く, but that kanji is outside the standard list and hiragana is much more common in everyday writing.

WHAT IT DOES AND DOESN'T MEAN:
つまずく is only the catching of the foot and the loss of balance. Whether you actually go down is a separate verb, which is why ⟦{転|ころ}ぶ→転ぶ：00863_korobu⟧ is so often added after it, as in example 1.

USAGE:
The physical meaning (sense 1) belongs to everyday conversation; the figurative meaning (sense 2) is frequent in news and business writing about projects, negotiations, and studies that ran into trouble early.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{石|いし}→石：02177_ishi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧つまずく: to trip on a stone
- ⟦{段差|だんさ}→段差：14742_dansa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧つまずく: to trip on a step
- ⟦{最初|さいしょ}→最初：00882_saisho⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一歩|いっぽ}→一歩：08890_ippo⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧つまずく: to stumble at the very first step
- ⟦{出|で}だし→出だし：30703_dedashi⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧つまずく: to stumble from the start
